name: Rui (nmn) Zhu
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, ADARx Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: ADRX), since January 2026
profile: Medicinal chemist and co-founder of San Diego RNA-therapeutics company ADARx Pharmaceuticals, where he led research from its December 2019 founding (VP R&D, then SVP Research) before becoming CTO in 2026. His stake stems from ADARx's 2026 IPO. Previously a senior scientist at Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals.
interesting_fact: ADARx, which he co-founded in 2019, develops RNA-editing and siRNA medicines and went public on Nasdaq in 2026 under the ticker ADRX.
deep_cut_fact: At Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals he co-led five siRNA discovery programs that advanced into Phase 1 clinical trials; he trained in chemistry at Nanjing University (B.S.) and Tsinghua University (Ph.D., organic chemistry).
notes: Low public profile; bio comes from the 2026 S-1/prospectus. Best route is via ADARx IR.

name: John A Cuomo
current_role: President, CEO and Director, VSE Corporation (Nasdaq: VSEC), since April 2019
profile: Aerospace-distribution executive who has run VSE since 2019, repositioning it as an aviation aftermarket distribution and MRO company. Before VSE he led Boeing Distribution Services (2018-19), KLX Aerospace Solutions (2014-18) and held senior roles at B/E Aerospace (2000-14). Also sits on the board of FDH Aero.
interesting_fact: He started his career as a commercial lawyer (M&A and litigation) at a multinational law firm before moving into aerospace in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in International Business, a J.D. from the University of Miami and an MBA from the University of Florida, and completed Harvard Business School's Advanced Management Program.
notes: Named a top transportation/logistics leader by Virginia Business (2023). Best route is VSE investor relations.

name: Alexander Merk
current_role: Founder, President and CIO, Merk Investments LLC (resigned as COO of ASA Gold and Precious Metals in June 2026)
profile: Alexander 'Axel' Merk founded Merk Investments, a gold- and currency-focused advisory firm that he grew to roughly $1B, and manages the Merk Funds and the ASA Gold and Precious Metals closed-end fund via Merk. He served as ASA's COO/principal executive officer from 2019 until resigning in June 2026. Known as a macro and hard-money commentator.
interesting_fact: He started the firm in Switzerland in 1994 by pooling money he had managed for friends since college, moved it to California in 2001, and launched the Merk Hard Currency Fund in 2005; he is described as a pioneer of strategic currency investing.
deep_cut_fact: Besides his Brown economics B.A. (magna cum laude) and computer-science M.Sc., his firm bio describes him as a long-distance runner, weekend vintner and private pilot; he wrote the 2009 book 'Sustainable Wealth'.
notes: Goes by 'Axel Merk'. Active on X and does frequent media/webinars, so likely receptive to podcasts. Avoid raising the June 2026 ASA resignation (cited control concerns).

name: Kwang Hooi Tan
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Flex Ltd. (Nasdaq: FLEX), since October 2024
profile: Malaysian-born manufacturing executive ('Hooi Tan') who has spent ~23 years at Flex, rising from China plant leadership to president of global operations and now COO, overseeing manufacturing, procurement, supply chain, IT and quality across ~100 sites in 30 countries. Flex is a major supplier of data-center power and liquid-cooling hardware.
interesting_fact: As COO he runs Flex's global factory network of roughly 100 facilities in 30 countries; Flex has been expanding data-center power and liquid-cooling capacity and announced plans in 2026 to spin off its cloud and power business.
deep_cut_fact: A Johor native whose father was an engineer, he was first drawn to filmmaking after seeing Star Wars before choosing engineering at Purdue; he started in 2000 as a test engineer at Solectron in Milpitas, then moved to China running sites in Suzhou, Nanjing and Shanghai.
notes: Goes by 'Hooi Tan'. Highly relevant to the data-center/energy theme (Flex power and liquid-cooling). He writes bylined pieces on Flex's site and mfg-outlook.com. Press email taken from a May 2026 release (an older filing lists press@flex.com).

name: Scott A Curtis
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Raymond James Financial (NYSE: RJF), since 2024; FINRA Board Industry Governor
profile: Wealth-management executive who joined Raymond James in 2003 to run its insurance group after 13 years at GE Financial Assurance, then led Raymond James Financial Services and, from 2018 to 2024, the Private Client Group, the firm's main wealth arm. As COO he oversees asset management, corporate real estate, marketing and strategic initiatives.
interesting_fact: He sits on FINRA's Board of Governors as a large-firm industry governor and chairs its Conflicts and Executive committees.
deep_cut_fact: A New Hampshire native, he grew up around Dartmouth football: his father coached there alongside future TD Ameritrade CEO Joe Moglia. He holds a Denison B.A. and a Michigan MBA, and serves on the board of the Chi Chi Rodriguez Youth Foundation.
notes: Chi Chi Rodriguez foundation detail is from FINRA bio page. Route via Raymond James media relations.

name: Eric J Gehringer
current_role: Executive Vice President-Operations, Union Pacific Railroad, since January 2021
profile: Railroad operations chief who joined Union Pacific in 2006 as a management trainee and rose through chief engineer, chief mechanical officer and SVP-Transportation roles before succeeding Jim Vena as head of operations in 2021. He leads transportation, engineering, mechanical, dispatching and customer care.
interesting_fact: He is an aerospace engineer by training (Saint Louis University) who worked at Northwest Airlines and DaimlerChrysler before switching to railroading.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the railroad he serves on the board of the Children's Nebraska Foundation and is a member of the U.S. Strategic Command Council; he also holds an MBA from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.
notes: Union Pacific is pursuing a merger with Norfolk Southern; his role could change. Route via UP media team.

name: Jon Kessler
current_role: Director, Phreesia, Inc. (NYSE: PHR) since April 2026; former President & CEO of HealthEquity (retired January 2025)
profile: Benefits-industry entrepreneur who ran WageWorks (2000-07), a pioneer in tax-advantaged employee spending accounts, then joined HealthEquity in 2009 and was its CEO 2014-2025, building it into the largest U.S. health savings account custodian (it acquired WageWorks in 2019). Now a public-company director at Phreesia.
interesting_fact: HealthEquity, which he led for over a decade, bought WageWorks, the company he had run earlier, in 2019, bringing his two ventures together.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a senior economist in Washington, D.C. specializing in employee benefits and environmental taxation during the Bush Sr. and Clinton administrations, and a benefits-taxation specialist at Arthur Andersen; he holds an MPP from Harvard Kennedy School.
notes: Has done podcasts before (Motley Fool Industry Focus 2019; Silicon Slopes). No published personal contact found; Phreesia or HealthEquity IR could forward. SEC 'Other' role at HQY reflects his post-CEO advisor status.

name: Mariano Bosch
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Director, Adecoagro S.A. (NYSE: AGRO), since 2002
profile: Argentine agricultural engineer who co-founded Adecoagro in 2002 and has run it since, building one of South America's largest food and renewable-energy producers (farmland, dairy, rice, sugar, ethanol, bioelectricity) across Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay. In 2025 stablecoin issuer Tether took a 70% controlling stake; Bosch remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Adecoagro became majority-owned by Tether, the stablecoin issuer, in April 2025, an unusual crypto-to-agriculture deal; the company also produces ethanol and renewable electricity from sugarcane.
deep_cut_fact: Before Adecoagro he founded and ran BLS Agribusiness (1995-2002), an agricultural consulting and farm-management firm; he is active in AACREA and Producir Conservando, groups that promote sustainable farming practices, and advises U.S. farmland investor Teays River.
notes: Good energy angle (sugarcane ethanol/bioelectricity) plus the Tether ownership story. Speaks at AS/COA events.

name: Jason Austin
current_role: Unknown; listed as a co-founder/director of Greensill Capital (UK) Ltd, which collapsed into insolvency in 2021
profile: Listed by Hurun and financial-data aggregators as one of the 2011 co-founders of supply-chain-finance firm Greensill Capital, alongside Lex and Peter Greensill and John Gorman, reportedly serving as president/director. Greensill filed for insolvency in 2021. No reliable current information found.
notes: Only thin aggregator sources (MarketScreener) link him to Greensill; a UK Companies House record for a 'Jason Richard Alexander Austin' shows a Greensill Capital Securities appointment but identity match is unconfirmed. Greensill's collapse is a sensitive topic; likely a poor podcast target.

name: Yang Qiujin
current_role: Chairperson and CEO of JUSDA; Chief Logistics and Trade Compliance Officer and Global Chief Campus Operation Officer, Hon Hai (Foxconn); rotating group CEO Apr 2025-Mar 2026
profile: Kathy Yang Chiu-chin (Yang Qiujin) is a supply-chain veteran who spent nearly two decades at UPS before joining Foxconn, where in 2015 she spun the internal logistics arm out as JUSDA, growing it from about $120M to $2.5B in revenue and raising a ~$356M Series A in 2019. She served as Foxconn's first female rotating CEO in 2025-26.
interesting_fact: She was Foxconn's first woman rotating CEO (April 2025 to March 2026) and led its 'Tariff Response Task Force' on supply-chain diversification; Fortune named her to its 100 Most Powerful Women Asia 2025 list.
deep_cut_fact: Before Foxconn she spent nearly two decades at UPS; reflecting on her year as rotating CEO she said it taught her to 'view the enterprise from a business-owner perspective'. She was also a WeQual Awards Asia-Pacific 2023 finalist.
notes: Known in English as Kathy Yang (Yang Chiu-chin). Hurun lists her as JUSDA 'founder' since she led its spin-out from Foxconn. No published personal/office contact found; route via Foxconn/JUSDA corporate communications.

name: Piyush Shah
current_role: Co-founder, InMobi; President & COO, Glance (InMobi's AI lock-screen platform)
profile: Indian entrepreneur who co-founded mobile-ad company InMobi (India's first unicorn) and served as its Chief Product Officer, building the InMobi Marketing Cloud and performance-advertising business. He now runs Glance, InMobi's AI-driven lock-screen content and commerce platform, as President & COO, and angel-invests in 20+ startups.
interesting_fact: He left a Deutsche Bank job to join a young Bangalore team building SMS-based search, which became InMobi; as chief product officer he later built its performance-advertising business, the company's biggest cash cow.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first venture, in education, at age 19 and was recognised by Business World as one of India's Innovative Youth Entrepreneurs; he studied engineering at Delhi College of Engineering and worked at Citigroup and Deutsche Bank before InMobi.
notes: Has done podcasts (Prime Venture Partners podcast, 2023) and spoke to YourStory in Aug 2026 on India's AI future, so likely open to interviews. Route via InMobi/Glance press pages.

name: Nathaniel Ru
current_role: Co-founder and Board Director, Sweetgreen, Inc. (NYSE: SG); retired as Chief Brand Officer effective January 1, 2026
profile: Co-founded salad chain Sweetgreen with Georgetown classmates Jonathan Neman and Nicolas Jammet, opening the first store in 2007; it grew to 280+ restaurants and listed on the NYSE in 2021. As Chief Brand Officer for ~20 years he led campaigns, collaborations and school programs; he retired from the role in January 2026 but remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Ru led Sweetgreen's sweetlife music and food festival and was named one of Fast Company's Most Creative People in Business and to Forbes' Next 50 CMOs list.
deep_cut_fact: Sweetgreen's first store, opened in August 2007 within three months of the founders' Georgetown graduation, was a tiny ~560-square-foot space on M Street; Ru also ran 'sweetgreen in schools' healthy-food education programs.
notes: Now has more free time after stepping back as CBO in Jan 2026; avoid the stock-decline framing some coverage used. Route via Sweetgreen press.

name: Oren Shoval
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Via Transportation (NYSE: VIA)
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded Via in 2012 with CEO Daniel Ramot and serves as CTO, building its algorithms for on-demand shared rides. Via evolved from a NYC ride-sharing service into software that powers public-transit, paratransit and school-transport systems for 800+ government and agency customers, and listed on the NYSE in 2025.
interesting_fact: The idea for Via came from Israel's 'sherut' shared taxis: Shoval couldn't get a seat on a fixed-route sherut and began thinking about a dynamic, software-routed version.
deep_cut_fact: Before Via he earned a PhD in systems biology at the Weizmann Institute of Science (2008-2012), after degrees in physics, math and electrical engineering.
notes: Bloomberg and Weizmann pages blocked direct fetch; facts from search snippets of those pages. Writes occasionally for TechCrunch. Route via Via press.

name: Francisco Montero
current_role: Co-founder, Cabify (Maxi Mobility); last publicly listed as Global Head of Settings / Global Ops (current role unverified)
profile: Francisco 'Paco' Montero is one of five co-founders of Madrid-based ride-hailing company Cabify (with Juan de Antonio, Vicente Pascual, Sam Lown and Adrian Merino), founded in 2011 and later valued at over $1B under parent Maxi Mobility. He worked across marketing, operations and 'excellence' functions and played a key role in Cabify's expansion into Latin America.
interesting_fact: Cabify founder Juan de Antonio gave the co-founder title to everyone who was there at the start of the company; Montero helped lead its early push into Latin America, which became Cabify's main market.
notes: Very low public profile; only brief mentions in Spanish press and Wellfound. No current role or contact verified. Route via Cabify press office if needed.
